IN THE HIGH COURT OF ANDHRA PRADESH: AMARAVATI  THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE SUBBA REDDY SATTI  WRIT PETITION No.25199 of 2020 Between:
Perumalla Kumari, W/o Devudu, aged about 50 years, Block No.34, Flat No.52, AMG Road, Rajeev Gruhakalpa,
Kakinada Urban, East Godavari District, Andhra Pradesh.

... Petitioner  AND The State of Andhra Pradesh, Rep. by its Principal Secretary (Revenue Department), Secretariat Buildings,
Velagapudi, Guntur District, Andhra Pradesh and five others.

... Respondents Counsel for the petitioners : Sri V. Sai Kumar Counsel for respondents : GP for Revenue  ORDER This writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India is filed seeking the following relief:
"... to issue a Writ or Order or Direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the Respondents 2 to 6 herein interfering with the possession of the petitioners in Survey No-66/1 to an extent of Ac.0.92 cents of Jagapathinagaram Panchayath, Kirlampudi Mandal, East Godavari District, without following the procedure established under law for acquisition of land under the SRS,
J Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 as illegal, arbitrary and also oppose to article 300-A of Constitution of India as well as oppose to principles of Natural Justice consequentially direct the respondents 2 to 6 herein not to interfere with the possession of the petitioners in Survey No.-66/1 to an extent of Ac.0.92 cents of Jagapathinagaram Panchayath, Kirlampudi Mandal, East Godavari District and to pass such other order or orders ..."
2.
In the affidavit, it was contended, interalia, that D-form patta was assigned in favour of petitioner's father-in-law on 12.08.1986, in respect of subject land.
Father-in-law of the petitioner cultivated the land till this death on 16.11.1999 and thereafter, husband of the petitioner succeeded the subject land.

After the death of petitioner's husband on 04.06.2020, petitioner along with her Perumalla Kumari vs The State Of Ap on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141499858/
1 family members has been cultivating the land.

sentences.text: Revenue authorities updated Record of Rights ('ROR').

Petitioner also made representation, dated 10.07.2017 to Revenue Divisional Officer i.e.
respondent No.2 for issuance of pattadar passbook ('PPB') and title deed ('TD') in her favour.
Respondent No.2, in turn, addressed letter, dated 17.07.2017 to Tahsildar requesting him to consider the petitioner's case and to pass appropriate orders.
While so, the respondent authorities are trying to SRS, J interfere with the possession of the petitioner over the subject land without issuing notice.
Hence, the writ petition.
3. Counter affidavit was filed on behalf of respondent No.4.

It was contended interlia that land of an extent of Ac.237-00 in survey No.66/1Y of Jagapthynagaram is classified as 'China Konda' i.e.
Government Poramboke.
Pattas were not assigned to any individual.
It is vacant on ground and no one is cultivating the land.

In the year, 2012, a case was filed before Vigilance and Enforcement Enquiry Department regarding forged pattas and PPBs obtained in respect of land in R.S.No.66/1Y of Jagapathinagaram village and verdict of case is awaited.
Thus, prayed to dismiss the writ petition.
4. This Court, by order, dated 31.12.2020 directed the parties to maintain status quo.

5. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Government Pleader for Revenue for respondent Nos.1 to 4 and 6.
6.

Learned counsel for the petitioner reiterated the contentions as per the averments in the writ affidavit and SRS, J learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue reiterated contentions as per the averments in the counter affidavit.

7. Along with the writ petition, D-form patta said to have been issued in favour of petitioner's father-in-law, in respect of land of an Ac.00-92 cents in survey No.66/1Y of Jagapathinagaram Panchayath, and the letter addressed by RDO to the Tahsildar directing to consider petitioner's case after conducting enquiry were filed.
8. The specific contention raised in the counter affidavit filed by respondent No.4, is that the patta said to have been issued in respect of the subject property is forged one.

It was further contended that vigilance enquiry was initiated with regard to forged pattas and PPBs in respect of land in survey No.66/1Y of Jagapathinagaram Panchayath and the verdict of case is awaited.
The enquiry was initiated in the year, 2012.
However, verdict has not been pronounced by the authority.

Since the petitioner's claim is based on the patta said to have been issued in favour of petitioner's father-in-law and since no verdict is rendered by the authority, the authorities shall not dispossess the petitioner without following due process of law.
SRS, J 9.
With the above direction, this writ petition is disposed of.
No costs.
This order will not preclude the authorities to proceed with the Vigilance enquiry in accordance with law.
As a sequel, pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand dismissed.
